body.statement:
For the common limit \(G_{\infty}\), the map \(\beta\mapsto q_{\alpha,\beta}\) is continuous, \(0<q_{\alpha,\beta}<\infty\), and
\[
0<\inf_{\beta\in\mathcal K}f_{\beta}(q_{\alpha,\beta})
\leq\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}f_{\beta}(q_{\alpha,\beta})<\infty.
\]
The coarea version \(\mathcal C(\beta,u)\) is continuous on a neighborhood of \(\{(\beta,q_{\alpha,\beta}):\beta\in\mathcal K\}\), and consequently \(\Gamma(\beta)\) is continuous on \(\mathcal K\).  If, in addition, \(I_{\mathrm{eff}}:\mathcal K\to\mathbb S_{++}^r\) is continuous, then \(B(\beta)=\operatorname{tr}\{\Gamma(\beta)I_{\mathrm{eff}}(\beta)^{-1}\}\) is continuous on \(\mathcal K\).
body.justification: Uniform coarea control makes the moving Gaussian acceptance boundary differentiable without adding a separate density assumption.
body.gap: Existing rerandomization limits use fixed quadratic forms; the uniform statement over an empirical-oracle chart is an auxiliary bridge to second order.
body.consumer: It supplies the stable quantile derivative needed to translate efficient pilot uncertainty into action regret.
body.proof_tex:
Set \(d=Fp\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}experiment\text{-}indexed\text{-}oracle\text{-}convergence}\), every \(G_{\infty}(\beta)\) is a limit of nonzero trace-normalized oracle scores.  Hence it is positive semidefinite with trace one.  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}oracle\text{-}rank}\), its rank is the fixed positive integer \(r_G\).  The max--min variational formulas for ordered eigenvalues show directly that they are continuous functions of a symmetric matrix in operator norm.  Continuity on compact \(\mathcal K\) and the constant-rank condition therefore give a number \(\lambda_->0\) such that every positive eigenvalue of every \(G_{\infty}(\beta)\) belongs to \([\lambda_-,1]\).

Rotational invariance of \(Z\) shows that
\[
 Z^{\mathsf T}G_{\infty}(\beta)Z
 \ \stackrel{d}{=}\ \sum_{j=1}^{r_G}\lambda_j(\beta)\xi_j^2,
\]
where the \(\xi_j\) are independent standard normal variables and the ordered positive eigenvalues \(\lambda_j(\beta)\) are continuous as an unordered multiset.  Convolution of the scaled chi-square densities shows that the right-hand side has a finite, continuous, strictly positive density at every \(u>0\).  The same convolution formula, dominated on compact subsets of \((0,\infty)\) by the bounds \(\lambda_j\in[\lambda_-,1]\), makes its distribution function and density jointly continuous in \((\beta,u)\).

The inequalities
\[
 \lambda_-\chi^2_{r_G}\leq\sum_{j=1}^{r_G}\lambda_j(\beta)\xi_j^2\leq\chi^2_{r_G}
\]
hold under the displayed coupling.  Since \(0<\alpha<1\), they place all \(q_{\alpha,\beta}\) in one compact subinterval of \((0,\infty)\).  Joint continuity and strict monotonicity of the distribution functions then imply continuity of \(\beta\mapsto q_{\alpha,\beta}\).  Joint continuity and positivity of the density on the compact quantile graph give
\[
 0<\min_{\beta\in\mathcal K}f_\beta(q_{\alpha,\beta})
 \leq\max_{\beta\in\mathcal K}f_\beta(q_{\alpha,\beta})<\infty.
\]

For completeness, continuity of the coarea moments can be checked without selecting eigenvectors globally.  The spectral projection onto the range of \(G_{\infty}(\beta)\) is continuous because the spectrum is uniformly separated from zero.  On a neighborhood of any fixed \(\beta\), projecting a fixed basis and applying Gram--Schmidt supplies continuous orthonormal frames for the range and null space.  In these coordinates the positive range block \(A_\beta\) has eigenvalues in \([\lambda_-,1]\).  On the level set \(r^{\mathsf T}A_\beta r=u\), make the change of variables
\[
 r=\sqrt u\,A_\beta^{-1/2}\omega,
 \qquad \omega\in\mathbb S^{r_G-1}.
\]
After the null Gaussian coordinates are integrated out, each denominator, first moment, and second moment in the definition of \(\mathcal C\) is an integral over the fixed unit sphere of a polynomial in \(\omega\), \(D_{\rho_a}G_{\infty}(\beta)\), and \(D_{\rho_b}G_{\infty}(\beta)\), multiplied by a Gaussian factor and continuous determinant powers of \(A_\beta\).  On a compact neighborhood of the quantile graph these integrands have one common integrable bound because \(u\) is bounded away from zero and the eigenvalues are in \([\lambda_-,1]\).  Dominated convergence therefore gives continuity of all raw coarea moments.  The denominator equals the strictly positive density just treated, so taking ratios and subtracting products proves continuity of \(\mathcal C(\beta,u)\).

The defining formula for \(\Gamma\), together with continuity of \(f\), \(q\), and \(\mathcal C\), proves continuity of \(\Gamma\).  Finally, under the additional condition stated in the narrowed claim, inversion is continuous on \(\mathbb S_{++}^r\); compactness keeps the inverse bounded.  Composition with matrix multiplication and trace then proves continuity of \(B\).  The frozen dependencies do not impose continuity of \(I_{\mathrm{eff}}\), which is why the last conclusion is necessarily conditional.
